archetypes.name: Background walkthrough
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a short walkthrough of the candidate's background that leads to this role.
archetypes.intent: Warm-up; observe structure and the career narrative.
strong_signals: 2-minute, chronological, ends with why this role
weak_signals: reads the CV line by line
probe_tree: Why did you move from X to Y?
What is the thread connecting these choices?

archetypes.name: CV claim verification ladder
archetypes.pattern: Pick one specific CV claim and ask the candidate to take you through it; then climb surface -> depth -> ownership -> evidence -> outcome.
archetypes.intent: Test whether a CV claim holds up and what the candidate personally did.
probe_tree: What exactly did you own?
How was the team structured, and what was your part?
Which decisions were yours?
What was the baseline and how did you measure the result?
How much of the result is attributable to your work?
What would you do differently?

archetypes.name: Ownership deep dive
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a time they took responsibility for an outcome beyond their brief.
probe_tree: What made it yours rather than someone else's?
What was the hardest moment?
What happened as a result?

archetypes.name: Quantified impact
archetypes.pattern: Ask about the most measurable impact they have had and how they know it was their impact.
probe_tree: What was the baseline?
Over what period?
What else changed at the same time?
How much was yours?

archetypes.name: Conflict
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a real disagreement with a colleague, manager or client and how it was resolved.
probe_tree: What was their reasoning?
What did you do first?
Where did you end up and how is the relationship now?

archetypes.name: Failure and learning
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a real failure or mistake, what their part was and what changed after.
probe_tree: What was your part in it?
What would you do differently?
Where have you applied that since?

archetypes.name: Leading or influencing
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a time they led people or influenced a decision without formal authority.
probe_tree: Who disagreed and why?
What did you do to bring them along?
What would have happened without you?

archetypes.name: Stakeholder situation
archetypes.pattern: Present a realistic role-specific situation with conflicting stakeholder demands and limited time.
probe_tree: What would you do in the first hour?
Who do you disappoint, and how?
What if your manager disagrees?

archetypes.name: Prioritisation trade-off
archetypes.pattern: Give 3-4 competing role-specific priorities with a constraint; ask what they do and what they drop.
probe_tree: You can only do one. Which?
What's the cost of not doing the others?
How would you communicate that?

archetypes.name: Concept explain & apply
archetypes.pattern: Ask the candidate to explain a role-critical concept and then apply it to a concrete situation from the role.
probe_tree: How would that change if <condition>?
Where does this break down?
Give me a real example.

archetypes.name: Applied functional scenario
archetypes.pattern: Present a realistic problem from the role's day-to-day and ask how they'd analyse and act.
probe_tree: What data would you look at first?
What would change your mind?
How would you measure success?

archetypes.name: Metric definition & diagnosis
archetypes.pattern: Ask how they would define success for a role-relevant initiative, then present a metric drop to diagnose.
probe_tree: The metric dropped 15% last week. Where do you start?
Which segment would you check first and why?

archetypes.name: Role-specific mini case
archetypes.pattern: Give a compact business problem relevant to the role with 1-2 numbers; ask for structure, analysis and a recommendation.
archetypes.intent: Structured problem solving and business judgment.
probe_tree: What's your hypothesis?
Walk me through the numbers.
So what do you recommend?
What's the biggest risk?

archetypes.name: Estimation
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a role-relevant estimate (market size, volume, capacity).
probe_tree: Why that approach?
Which assumption matters most?
How would you sanity-check this?

archetypes.name: Debugging walkthrough
archetypes.pattern: Describe a realistic failure in the candidate's stack and ask how they'd diagnose it.
probe_tree: What do you check first?
The logs show nothing. Now what?
How do you stop it recurring?

archetypes.name: System design (verbal)
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a high-level design of a role-relevant system, then deep-dive one component and its trade-offs.
probe_tree: What are the scale assumptions?
Where is the bottleneck?
What happens when X fails?

archetypes.name: Technical concept depth ladder
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a technical concept the role relies on and descend: concept -> how it works -> implementation -> trade-offs -> limitations.
probe_tree: How does it work under the hood?
When would you not use it?
What breaks at scale?

archetypes.name: Technical project deep dive
archetypes.pattern: Pick a technical project from the CV and probe architecture, their decisions and trade-offs.
probe_tree: Draw me the architecture in words.
Which decision was yours?
What would you change now?

archetypes.name: Motivation & role fit
archetypes.pattern: Ask why this role/company now and what they understand the role to involve.
strong_signals: specific to the company and role
probe_tree: What do you think the first 90 days look like?
What would make you leave this role?

archetypes.name: Company & role simulation
archetypes.pattern: Use JD-stated company context to pose a problem this role would face at this company.
archetypes.intent: Applying understanding of the company to the role.
probe_tree: What would you prioritise first here?
What do you think is the biggest risk for this business?

archetypes.name: Hiring-manager judgment
archetypes.pattern: Ask what they'd do in their first weeks given a concrete messy situation in the team.
probe_tree: What would you not touch in the first month?
How would you know it's working?

archetypes.name: Pressure pushback
archetypes.pattern: Challenge the candidate's previous answer professionally: ask for evidence, add a constraint, or force a choice.
archetypes.intent: Defending reasoning with evidence; updating when wrong.
probe_tree: I'm not convinced. What evidence do you have?
You have two weeks, not two months. What changes?
You can only do one. Which?

archetypes.name: Contradiction clarification
archetypes.pattern: Neutrally point to two statements that do not match and ask the candidate to clarify.
archetypes.intent: Resolve an inconsistency without assuming bad faith.
probe_tree: Help me reconcile those two.

archetypes.name: Closing
archetypes.pattern: Invite the candidate's questions and close the interview.

archetypes.name: Learning fast
archetypes.pattern: Ask about something they had to learn quickly for real work and how they got up to speed.
archetypes.intent: How the candidate learns under time pressure.
expected_evidence: what had to be learned and why
how fast and how they knew it was enough
strong_signals: applied it to a real outcome
probe_tree: How did you decide what to learn first?
How did you know you were good enough to rely on it?
What would you do differently next time?

archetypes.name: Feedback
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a piece of critical feedback they received and what they changed because of it.
weak_signals: feedback that is a hidden compliment
probe_tree: How did you react in the moment?
What did you change the week after?
How do you know it stuck?

archetypes.name: Ambiguity
archetypes.pattern: Ask about making progress on a problem with little information or direction.
archetypes.intent: Initiative and judgement when the path is unclear.
probe_tree: What did you do in the first two days?
What assumption did you make, and how did you test it?
What would have changed your mind?

archetypes.name: Integrity under pressure
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a time they were pressured to cut a corner and what they did.
archetypes.intent: Integrity and judgement when the easy path is wrong.
probe_tree: Who was pushing, and why?
What did it cost you to hold the line?
Would you do the same again?

archetypes.name: Pressure & setbacks
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a period of heavy pressure or a real setback and how they responded.
weak_signals: heroic overwork as the only answer
probe_tree: What did you drop, and how did you decide?
Who did you tell, and when?
What would you do differently?

archetypes.name: Persuading with evidence
archetypes.pattern: Ask for a time they changed someone's mind with evidence rather than authority.
strong_signals: tailors the evidence to the audience
probe_tree: What was their original view based on?
What evidence moved them?
What did you do when they pushed back?

archetypes.name: Team & collaboration
archetypes.pattern: Ask about the candidate's part in making a team work — or helping a struggling teammate.
probe_tree: What did you personally do differently from the others?
How did the other person respond?
What changed for the team?

archetypes.name: Customer / user focus
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a customer or user problem they went out of their way to solve.
expected_evidence: what they did beyond the brief
probe_tree: How did you find out what they really needed?
What did it cost, and was it worth it?
What changed afterwards?

archetypes.name: An idea that got adopted
archetypes.pattern: Ask about an idea of theirs that was actually implemented and how they got it adopted.
archetypes.intent: Initiative, creativity and the ability to get things adopted.
expected_evidence: the idea and the problem it solved
probe_tree: Who resisted, and why?
How did you test it before rolling it out?
How did you measure the result?

archetypes.name: Interests & hobbies
archetypes.pattern: Ask about one interest or hobby the candidate lists — how deep it goes and what it has taught them.
archetypes.intent: The person behind the CV: depth, curiosity and transferable lessons.
strong_signals: links a lesson to how they work without forcing it
probe_tree: How did you get into it?
What's the hardest thing you've done in it?
Where does that show up in how you work?

archetypes.name: Leading beyond the job
archetypes.pattern: Ask about a position of responsibility, club, event or competition from the CV: their part, the hard part, the result.
archetypes.intent: Leadership and ownership outside formal work.
strong_signals: handles people they could not command
probe_tree: What did you personally own?
What was the hardest moment, and what did you do?
What would you do differently?

archetypes.name: Achievement beyond work
archetypes.pattern: Ask about an achievement outside their job or degree that they are proud of and what it took.
archetypes.intent: Drive and persistence in self-chosen goals.
probe_tree: What nearly made you stop?
How did you prepare?
What did it teach you?

archetypes.name: Self-awareness
archetypes.pattern: Ask how people who worked closely with them would describe them, including what they could do better.
expected_evidence: what they are doing about it
weak_signals: weakness that is a strength in disguise
probe_tree: Can you give me an example of that?
What are you doing about it right now?
Who would disagree with that description?

archetypes.name: A recent business story
archetypes.pattern: Use one recent, real news item (given to you) or let the candidate pick one; ask what it means and what a company should do.
archetypes.intent: Business awareness and the ability to turn news into a judgement.
strong_signals: goes beyond the headline to implications
probe_tree: Who wins and who loses from this?
What would you do in the next quarter if you ran one of these companies?
What would change your view?

archetypes.name: Industry trend
archetypes.pattern: Ask for one trend changing the role's industry and which companies win or lose because of it.
archetypes.intent: Understanding of the industry the role sits in.
probe_tree: Why now?
Which company is best placed, and why?
What does that mean for someone in this role?

archetypes.name: A strategic move
archetypes.pattern: Ask which company is making a smart strategic move right now, why, and what the risk is.
probe_tree: What's the biggest risk in that move?
What would you watch to know it's working?
What would a competitor do in response?
